items.entity: MBB half-beam design domain (length, height, aspect ratio)
items.description: Sec. 3.4 gives only element counts HNex×HNey (60×20, 120×40, 300×100). No physical length, height or hexagon size is stated. 'rfill = 2.4√3 … i.e., 0.04 times the maximum length' implies a length of HNex·√3, but the height (the hexagon row pitch set on lines 20–22, which is deferred to [1]) is not given. Fig. 1(a) shows the domain but cannot be seen, so the rectangle aspect ratio for a structured grid is not fixed.
readings: L:H = 3:1, taking HNex:HNey literally (e.g. 60×20 square cells)
L = HNex·√3, H = 1.5·HNey (regular unit-side hexagons): L:H = 2√3 ≈ 3.46:1 (≈103.9×30 for 60×20)
Full bounding box of the zigzag honeycomb: L = HNex·√3, H = 1.5·HNey+0.5 (≈103.9×30.5, ≈3.41:1)

items.entity: Hexagonal element geometry and the equivalent structured-grid resolution
items.description: Sec. 3.1 sends the reader to [1] and Fig. 1(b) for the hexagon shape and size, row staggering, boundary shape and the removal of hanging nodes for even HNey (all three meshes have even HNey). No node coordinates are given. The structured-grid cell size and count must therefore be chosen, and the text says the ft=0 result (Fig. 2(a)) is mesh-dependent. That checkerboard-free ft=0 result also depends on hexagonal edge connectivity.
readings: Keep HNey rows with the hexagon aspect ratio: ≈69×20 (139×40, 346×100)

items.description: Sec. 3.4 lists three meshes. The Fig. 2 caption assigns only the rows to ft=0/1/2 and never says which column belongs to which mesh. Fig. 2(a) is presumably the coarsest mesh, but this is not stated.

Sec. 2 says only that Fig. 1(a) shows 'the symmetric half-design domain … with the pertinent boundary conditions'. fixeddofs (line 37) is not listed for the MBB. The text does not say which vertical edge is the symmetry cut, or which nodes of the staggered honeycomb edge are constrained. The mirrored choice gives a mirror-image layout.
readings: Left edge: ux = 0 at every node on x = 0
Right edge: ux = 0 at every node on x = L (mirrored set-up)

items.entity: Support at the outer-end bottom corner
items.description: The end support type appears only in Fig. 1(a). The text does not say whether it is a vertical roller (the classical MBB) or a pin. A pin adds horizontal restraint and changes the load path.

items.entity: Location and extent of the outer-end bottom support
items.description: Shown only in Fig. 1(a). It could be the single bottom corner node opposite the symmetry edge. On the zigzag hexagon bottom edge it could also be the lowest nearby node or a few nodes.
readings: Single bottom corner node at x = L
Lowest bottom-edge node nearest x = L (half a hexagon in from the corner)
Several bottom-edge nodes near x = L

items.description: Sec. 2 places the load only through Fig. 1(a), and the force indices (row/col/data, line 34) are not given for the MBB. All three meshes have even HNey, so hanging nodes are removed (Sec. 3.1), but the text does not say where they are. If the top corner node is one of them, the load must go on a neighbouring node.
readings: Top corner node on the symmetry edge (x = 0, y = H)
Top corner on the opposite edge (mirrored set-up)
Nearest remaining top node, half a hexagon width from the symmetry edge

items.description: Fig. 1(a) only. Sec. 3.2 describes setting 'a non-zero force value' at given indices, which suggests a single nodal force, but the MBB force vector is never written out.
readings: Force spread over a few top-edge nodes next to the symmetry edge

items.description: The direction and sign of F appear only in Fig. 1(a). The MBB convention is vertical and downward. Reversing the sign changes neither the compliance nor the layout.
|F| is not stated for the MBB (the Sec. 4 examples use ±1 and ±2). The reported C values (e.g. 298.92) scale with |F|².
readings: |F| = 0.5 (half of a unit full-beam load at the symmetry plane)

items.description: Sec. 3.2 says E0 and Emin are 'stored' on lines 12–13 but gives no values. Sec. 2 gives only Emin/E0 = 1e-9 and 'k0 … with E(ρj)=1'.
Sec. 3.2 says KE is built from Wachspress shape functions under plane stress, but ν is never given.
The out-of-plane thickness is not stated. It only scales K and C.

items.entity: Filter switch ft (sensitivity vs density filter)
items.description: Sec. 3.3 says 'sensitivity filtering (ft=1), density filtering (ft=1)', but later says xPhys is filtered only for ft=2. Sec. 3.4 and Fig. 2 use ft = 0, 1, 2. This affects Fig. 2(d–i); Fig. 2(a) is ft=0 (no filter).
readings: ft=1 sensitivity filter, ft=2 density filter
ft=1 density filter, ft=2 sensitivity filter

items.entity: Filter radius rfill in structured-grid units
items.description: In Sec. 3.4, rfill = 2.4√3 / 4.8√3 / 12√3 is given in hexagon coordinate units that are never defined, and explained as '0.04 times the maximum length'. How many cells it covers depends on the cell size chosen. It is not used for Fig. 2(a) (ft=0).
readings: rmin = 0.04·L (2.4 cells on a 60-cell length, 4.16 cells on a 104-cell length)
rmin = 2.4√3 ≈ 4.16 cell widths on a 60-cell-long grid (literal value)

items.description: Lines 76–77 build HHs 'with indices based on the distances in DD', and dc is 'updated as per different ft'. The weight function, the neighbour test (< or ≤ rfill) and the form of the sensitivity filter (density weighting, small lower bound in the denominator) are only cited from [7] and [10]. Not relevant for ft=0.
readings: Linear cone weights max(0, rfill−d); 99-line sensitivity filter dc = H(x·dc)/(Hs·max(1e-3,x)); density filter with chain rule on dc and dv
Linear cone weights; sensitivity filter without density weighting

items.description: Sec. 3.3 says 'move' is defined on line 80 but gives no value.

items.entity: Stopping criteria (maxiter and tolerance on change)
items.description: maxiter and change are defined on line 80, and 'termination conditions are monitored by change', but neither the threshold nor the iteration limit is given. This matters most for the slowly converging unfiltered run (Fig. 2(a)).
OcC and the search interval inL (lines 101–114) are described only in words. The damping exponent, the initial bracket and the bisection tolerance are not given.
